body: The schema hard-codes `embedding vector(1024)`, but the default embedding backend in `src/core/embedding.ts` is OpenAI (1536 dims) when `OLLAMA_URL` is not set. That combination will cause inserts/searches to fail due to pgvector dimension mismatch. Either keep the default schema at 1536, or make schema initialization/migrations conditional on the selected provider (and require `OLLAMA_URL` when using 1024).

`src/core/db.ts` / `src/core/postgres-engine.ts` initialize Postgres using the embedded schema in `src/core/schema-embedded.ts`, not by reading `src/schema.sql` at runtime. After changing `src/schema.sql`, `schema-embedded.ts` needs to be regenerated (per its header) or the Postgres engine will continue using the old 1536-dimension defaults.
```suggestion
-- Change dimension below and re-run import with --fresh to re-embed existing data.
-- IMPORTANT: Postgres initialization uses the embedded schema in
-- src/core/schema-embedded.ts, so after editing this file you must
-- regenerate src/core/schema-embedded.ts as described in that file's header,
-- or the runtime schema may continue using stale dimensions/defaults.
```

These config defaults are set to `bge-m3`/`1024`, but the application currently does not use these values to select the embedding provider/dimensions (and chunk inserts default `model` to `text-embedding-3-large` in the engines). This makes the stored config misleading unless the runtime is updated to actually read/enforce it.

`content_chunks.embedding` is defined as `vector(1024)`, but `src/core/embedding.ts` uses OpenAI embeddings (1536 dims) by default unless `OLLAMA_URL` is set. With the current defaults this will fail at insert/query time due to dimension mismatch. Consider leaving the default at 1536 or making schema selection/migration depend on the active embedding provider.

The schema seeds `embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions` as `bge-m3`/`1024`, but current chunk upserts in both engines supply `chunk.model || 'text-embedding-3-large'`, so the DB defaults/config won’t match what actually gets written unless callers start setting `chunk.model` based on the selected backend.
```suggestion
  ('embedding_model', 'text-embedding-3-large'),
  ('embedding_dimensions', '3072'),
```

`DIMENSIONS` is set to 1024 and exported as `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS`, but the OpenAI path explicitly requests 1536 dimensions. When `USE_OLLAMA` is false, the exported dimensions/model values won’t reflect what `embedBatchOpenAI()` actually produces, which can lead to incorrect schema/config choices elsewhere. Consider exporting provider-specific constants (OPENAI_DIMENSIONS/OLLAMA_DIMENSIONS) or computed `ACTIVE_MODEL`/`ACTIVE_DIMENSIONS` based on `USE_OLLAMA`, and use those consistently.

`EmbeddingConfig.dimensions` is declared optional, but `getEmbeddingConfig()` always returns a number (defaults to `DEFAULT_DIMENSIONS` even when `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` is unset). That means the downstream request builders will always include `dimensions/output_dimension` (because 1536 is truthy), including for Voyage. If the intent is that dimensions are only overridden when explicitly provided, return `dimensions: undefined` when the env var is unset (and consider making the default provider-aware). Also prefer checking `config.dimensions !== undefined` and validate it’s a positive integer to avoid silently skipping `0` due to the current truthy check.

`model: embeddingConfig.model` is being written for *every* chunk in the page, including chunks that already had embeddings and are not being re-embedded in this run. Because `upsertChunks` updates `model = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.model, content_chunks.model)`, this will overwrite the stored model for unchanged embeddings and can make metadata inaccurate. Consider only setting `model` for chunks whose embedding is newly computed/updated, and leaving it `undefined` for the others so the existing value is preserved.

In the `--all/--stale` path, `model: embeddingConfig.model` is applied to every chunk even when `staleOnly` and the chunk’s embedding is left unchanged. This will overwrite the existing `content_chunks.model` value for previously-embedded chunks and can mislabel embeddings created with a different model/provider. Only set `model` when you are also setting a new embedding for that chunk (or otherwise preserve the existing model).

This static import of `getEmbeddingConfig` causes `../src/core/embedding.ts` to be loaded before the `mock.module('../src/core/embedding.ts', ...)` call later in the file, which can prevent the mock from taking effect for `runEmbed`. Also, the current mock only exports `embedBatch`, but `runEmbed` now imports `getEmbeddingConfig` too—so under the mock, `getEmbeddingConfig` may be missing and cause runtime failures. Consider switching to a dynamic import for `getEmbeddingConfig` after mocking, or updating the module mock to also export `getEmbeddingConfig` (e.g., by forwarding to the real implementation).

`EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` is parsed and allowed to differ from 1536 here, but the database schema and engines currently hardcode `content_chunks.embedding` as `vector(1536)` and insert/search casts as `::vector`. If a user sets dimensions (e.g. 1024), inserts and vector search will fail due to dimension mismatch. Either constrain/validate `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` to 1536 for now, or include the necessary schema/index migration + engine adjustments to support variable vector dimensions.

With `getPage/getChunks/getTags/...` now defaulting to `source_id='default'` when `sourceId` is omitted, the interface becomes inconsistent with `listPages()` / `getAllSlugs()` (which currently return entries across *all* sources). Callers that iterate via `listPages()` and then call `getChunks(slug)` / `getTags(slug)` (e.g. embed/export flows) will silently operate only on the default source for non-default pages. Consider adding source scoping to `listPages`/`getAllSlugs` (or including `source_id` in the returned `Page` shape) so multi-source callers can preserve source context end-to-end.

This change introduces source-scoped import behavior, but there doesn’t appear to be a regression test asserting that importing with `sourceId` writes/updates pages, tags, chunks, and versions under that source (and not under `default`). Given the existing test coverage around import/sync and multi-source behavior, adding a focused test here would prevent this bug from recurring (ideally covering both PGLite and Postgres paths if the test suite supports it).

`defaultProfileForRecipe()` ignores the configured `prefer` source class. If a user sets `prefer: 'openclaw-openai'` for the OpenAI recipe but omits `profile`, `profile` will default to `openclaw-codex` because the recipe id is `openai`, which is inconsistent with the selected source. Consider defaulting the profile based on `providerConfig.prefer` (or passing `prefer` into the defaulting helper) so `prefer` and the default profile stay aligned.

`missingResolution()` sets `credentialKey` to the OpenClaw profile name when `prefer` is an OpenClaw source. That value is later used by `gateway.ts#requireAuth()` to build the user-facing error message, resulting in messages like "OpenAI embedding requires openclaw-codex" instead of referencing the actual required credential (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`) or the selected auth mechanism. Consider keeping `credentialKey` as the actual env var key (or leaving it undefined) and putting the expected profile name into `meta` / a dedicated field so error/status messages remain accurate.

When `readOpenClawAuthRecord()` fails (file missing, unreadable, or invalid JSON), it returns `null` and `resolveOpenClawProfileAuth()` always reports "profile ... not found". This can produce misleading diagnostics for parse/permission errors. Consider surfacing a more specific missingReason for read/parse failures (e.g., distinguish ENOENT vs JSON parse error) so users get actionable setup guidance.

The `Recipe.auth_env` doc comment is now misleading: it says "first is required, rest are optional", but the type has explicit `required` vs `optional` arrays and the resolver treats `required` as a priority-ordered set of acceptable keys. Please update the comment (or rename fields) so it matches the actual semantics and avoids confusion for future recipe additions.

In `providers env`, `openclawSatisfied` marks `OPENAI_API_KEY` as satisfied solely based on `GBRAIN_OPENCLAW_CODEX_AUTH=1`, even if no auth path/dir is configured or no readable token exists. This can mislead users into thinking setup is complete. Suggest checking `resolveOpenClawCodexAuthToken(process.env)` (or at least verifying `GBRAIN_OPENCLAW_AUTH_PATH`/`GBRAIN_OPENCLAW_AUTH_DIR` points to an existing file) and printing a clearer status when opt-in is enabled but no profile/token is found.

`isAvailable()` now calls `resolveOpenAIApiKey()`, which may do synchronous filesystem reads (`existsSync`/`readFileSync`) via `resolveOpenClawCodexAuthToken`. `isAvailable('embedding')` is called in hot paths (e.g. on every search and put_page), so this can add blocking I/O and latency on each request when OpenClaw auth opt-in is enabled. Consider resolving/memoizing the OpenAI credential once at `configureGateway()` time (or caching the resolution result in module state reset on `configureGateway/resetGateway`) so `isAvailable()` stays O(1) and avoids sync disk I/O.

`resolveOpenAIApiKey()` mutates `cfg.credential_sources` as a side effect while performing token resolution. Since this function is called from both `isAvailable()` and provider instantiation, it makes “availability checks” non-pure and can lead to repeated re-resolution work. If you add caching, consider separating “resolve credentials” from “record credential source info” (or only recording once) to avoid surprising state changes during `isAvailable()` calls.

These tests create temporary directories via `mkdtempSync` but never remove them. Over time this can clutter the OS temp dir (and can matter in CI runners that reuse workspaces). Consider tracking created dirs and cleaning them up in a `try/finally`, `afterEach`, or using `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` at the end of each test.

`envReady()` treats `GBRAIN_OPENCLAW_CODEX_AUTH=1` as “ready” for OpenAI even when no `GBRAIN_OPENCLAW_AUTH_PATH`/`GBRAIN_OPENCLAW_AUTH_DIR` is set or when the profile file can’t be parsed. This can make `gbrain providers list/explain` report ✓ ready and even recommend OpenAI, while gateway calls will still fail. Consider reusing the same resolver logic as the gateway (e.g. call `resolveOpenClawCodexAuthToken(process.env)` and only return true when it returns a token), or at minimum require a configured path/dir and verify the file exists.

This only fixes stdin handling for shared operations. `handleCliOnly('report')` still dispatches to `src/commands/report.ts`, and that code still does `readFileSync('/dev/stdin', 'utf-8')`, so `echo ... | gbrain report ...` will continue to fail on Windows with the same ENOENT this PR is addressing here.

This changes a platform-specific stdin regression path, but the CLI test suite does not exercise piped stdin for `gbrain put` (or the new `fstatSync(0)` guard). Without a spawn-based regression test that writes to fd 0, it's easy for a future refactor to reintroduce the Windows/pipe breakage unnoticed.

Good catch — fixed in a2b5773.

`src/commands/report.ts:44` had the same `readFileSync('/dev/stdin', 'utf-8')` pattern (introduced separately, not via `parseOpArgs`). I applied the same fd 0 + `fstatSync(0)` guard there. Verified: `echo body | gbrain report --type X --title Y` now succeeds on Windows with piped stdin and short-circuits cleanly with the existing "No content provided" error when stdin is `ignore`d.

Also added a `git grep` source-invariant test (`test/cli-stdin-cross-platform.test.ts`, second `describe` block) that walks `src/` for `'/dev/stdin'` string literals — if any future code path adds a third site, it fails the build. I confirmed the invariant fires by temporarily reverting either patched file: the test catches it.

Agreed — added in a2b5773.

`test/cli-stdin-cross-platform.test.ts` spawns the actual CLI via `Bun.spawn` and validates four functional cases against `gbrain report` (chosen because it doesn't need a DB connection, so the test is fast and hermetic):

- piped stdin → content reaches the file via fd 0
- ignored stdin (`stdin: 'ignore'`) → exits with the existing "No content provided" error, no block, no crash
- `--content` argv → takes precedence over piped stdin
- `--help` with piped stdin → still exits 0 cleanly

Plus the source-invariant `git grep` test mentioned in the other thread, which guards against new code paths reintroducing the POSIX-only pattern.

I deliberately wired the spawn helper around `Bun.argv[0]` (the absolute bun path) and `fileURLToPath()` for cwd/script paths — bare `'bun'` and `new URL().pathname` both fail on Windows, and the existing `cli.test.ts` doesn't exercise this on Windows so it slipped through. Tests now pass on Windows + Bun 1.3.13. Should also pass cleanly on macOS/Linux since the new fstatSync guard accepts the same FIFO/file/socket cases the old `!isTTY` was handling there.

`opts.sourceId ? ... : undefined` treats an empty-string source id as “no source”. The codebase explicitly allows/pins `sourceId === ''` (see cycle sourceId resolution regression tests), so this will read/delete from the default source instead of the intended empty-id source. Prefer checking `opts.sourceId !== undefined` or just always passing `{ sourceId: opts.sourceId }` and letting engines default when it’s undefined.

Same empty-string `sourceId` issue as above: this delete path will target `default` when `opts.sourceId === ''`. Use an undefined-check (or pass `{ sourceId: opts.sourceId }` unconditionally) so deletes are correctly scoped for all valid source ids.

`opts.sourceId ? { sourceId: opts.sourceId } : undefined` drops empty-string source ids. The repo has tests that explicitly allow `sourceId === ''`, so this would incorrectly import/read/write against `default`. Use an undefined-check or pass `{ sourceId: opts.sourceId }` unconditionally so empty ids are preserved.

Same empty-string `sourceId` bug for code-file imports: the truthy check will drop `sourceId === ''` and incorrectly operate on `default`. Use `opts.sourceId !== undefined` (or pass `{ sourceId: opts.sourceId }` unconditionally) so source scoping is preserved.

Now that `createVersion` is source-scoped, `getVersions()` (and likely `revertToVersion()`) become ambiguous in multi-source brains when the same slug exists in multiple sources: callers can’t request versions for a non-default source, and results may mix sources. Consider threading an optional `{ sourceId?: string }` through `getVersions`/`revertToVersion` as well and filtering by `p.source_id` in both engines for consistency.

The GetPageOpts doc comment says “When omitted, page CRUD uses the default source”, but this type is specifically for `getPage / softDeletePage / restorePage`. Suggest clarifying it to “When omitted, getPage uses the default source” (and document other CRUD defaults elsewhere if needed) to avoid misleading API consumers.

PostgresEngine schema templating updates the vector column dimensions but leaves the seeded config row `('embedding_dimensions', '1536')` unchanged in SCHEMA_SQL. For non-default brains (e.g. 2048d), `engine.getConfig('embedding_dimensions')` will still report 1536 and commands like migrate-engine that copy config keys will propagate the wrong value. Consider templating/replacing the config insert value as well (similar to how embedding_model is replaced).

The schema SQL templating interpolates `model` directly into a quoted SQL literal (`'${model}'`) without escaping. If the configured model string contains a single quote, schema init will generate invalid SQL (and it also opens an injection vector if untrusted config is ever used). Escape single quotes (e.g. doubling them) before substitution, as done in getPGLiteSchema().

`defaultProfileForRecipe()` selects the default OpenClaw profile solely based on `recipe.id`, ignoring the requested `providerConfig.prefer`. If a user sets `prefer: 'openclaw-openai'` for the OpenAI recipe and does not explicitly set `profile`, the resolver will still look up `openclaw-codex` while reporting the source as `openclaw-openai`, producing inconsistent behavior/metadata. Consider choosing the default profile based on `providerConfig.prefer` (or passing `prefer` into the default-profile selection) so `openclaw-openai` actually uses the `openclaw-openai` profile by default.

When OpenClaw auth is preferred but the profile is missing, `missingResolution()` sets `credentialKey` to the profile name (e.g. `openclaw-codex`). `requireAuth()` then formats the primary error as "<Provider> <action> requires openclaw-codex.", which reads like an env var name and is confusing. Consider either (a) distinguishing profile-vs-env in `credentialKey`, or (b) changing the error text to mention "OpenClaw profile" when `resolution.source === 'missing'` and the preferred auth mode is OpenClaw.

`gbrain import-media` does not appear to exist in the current CLI (there is `gbrain import`, but it imports markdown directories). This reference will confuse adapter authors; either update to an existing ingestion command/path or reword to describe a generic “import/extraction ingest” consumer without naming a non-existent command.

The error response example omits `protocolVersion`, while the success response includes it and the contract otherwise keys on that version string. Consider including `protocolVersion` (and possibly a stable error schema) on error responses too, so clients can reliably route/validate failures.

The suggested credential configuration shape uses a `provider_auth` key, but that key isn’t present in GBrain’s config model (current config supports fields like `openai_api_key`, `anthropic_api_key`, and env-var precedence). Either align this example with the real config surface or clearly label it as a proposed/future adapter-to-core contract to avoid sending readers to a non-existent setting.

When `--content-file` is omitted and the page already exists, `existingPageContent()` re-serializes the page with `tags: []`. Because tags are stored separately from `page.frontmatter` (and `parseMarkdown()` strips `tags` out of frontmatter), this path will erase all existing tags on re-import by causing `parseMediaPageContent()` to see zero tags and then removing them in the import transaction. Consider fetching `await engine.getTags(slug)` and passing those tags into `serializeMarkdown(...)`, or otherwise preserving existing tags when regenerating content.

The directory whitelist comment block above DIR_PATTERN is now out of date: it enumerates canonical dirs + a few extensions but doesn’t mention the newly added prefixes (incidents, releases, adrs, retros, postmortems). Please update the comment so future edits don’t miss these and reviewers can tell which dirs are intentionally supported.

This change adds new top-level dirs to link extraction, but there are currently no unit tests covering wikilinks/markdown links/bare-slug matches for these prefixes (e.g. incidents/... or releases/...). Please add at least a couple of assertions in test/link-extraction.test.ts to lock in the new behavior and prevent future regressions of the whitelist.

`JSON.parse(stdout.slice(firstJson))` will throw if the CLI prints any non-JSON *after* the envelope (or prints braces in a preface line), because it tries to parse from the first "{" to the end of stdout. Consider extracting/parsing the last JSON object (or scanning newline-delimited stdout for the last line that parses as JSON) and wrapping `JSON.parse` errors into an `AIConfigError`/`AITransientError` with a helpful hint (including a truncated stdout/stderr preview)."

Passing `env` directly to `Bun.spawn` can unintentionally drop the parent process environment (e.g., `HOME`, `XDG_*`, `PATH`), depending on runtime semantics, which may break Composio CLI behavior (it typically reads auth/config from the user's home directory). Prefer constructing the child environment by merging with the current process environment and omitting `undefined` values (e.g., merge `process.env` + `cfg.env`), so the CLI has the expected baseline environment.

`cost_per_1m_tokens_usd: 0.13` is accurate for `text-embedding-3-large` but not for `text-embedding-3-small` (which has a lower per-1M token price). If this field is used for cost estimation, this recipe will overestimate costs for the small model. Consider either (a) splitting this into per-model pricing metadata, (b) declaring separate touchpoints/entries per model, or (c) omitting `cost_per_1m_tokens_usd` when multiple models with different prices are listed.

The new hard-coded `COMPOSIO_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE` is an unexplained magic number and is independent of the recipe’s declared token budget (`max_batch_tokens`). Consider documenting the constraint (e.g., Composio/OpenAI CLI stability limits), or moving this limit into the recipe touchpoint config so it’s discoverable and adjustable per provider/model without editing gateway code.

The new `composio-openai` embed path has a happy-path test, but key parsing/error behaviors aren’t covered: (1) stdout containing trailing non-JSON after the envelope, (2) an envelope that includes the payload inline (not `storedInFile`), and (3) JSON parse failures producing a user-oriented `AIConfigError`/`AITransientError` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. Adding targeted tests for these cases would lock in the intended robustness of the Composio CLI integration.

verifyConversionManifestLinkage treats the absence of any conversion manifest for an existing file as {status:'corrupt', reasons:['MAPPING_MISSING']}. This is inconsistent with inspectConversionFile(), which reports the same condition as state:'legacy_absent', and it also overloads the 'MAPPING_MISSING' reason code for a missing receipt (not a missing mapping). Returning an explicit legacy/absent status (and empty reasons) would make the linkage API behavior unambiguous and aligned with inspectConversionFile.

Chunk-bound validation currently SELECTs every matching chunk_index just to compare the row count. For large chunk ranges this can be unnecessarily expensive and increases memory/transfer; a COUNT(*) query is sufficient for the invariant being checked.

boundedValue() applies the settings allowlist (allowedKeys) to every nested object it traverses, not just the top-level settings keys. This means settings like { format: { kind: 'png' } } will be rejected because 'kind' is not in SETTINGS_KEYS, even though the top-level key is allowlisted. If the intent is to allow nested structure under allowlisted top-level keys, the allowlist should only be enforced at the first object level where it's supplied.

Fixed in f60e0f85. `verifyConversionManifestLinkage` now returns `status: legacy_absent`, null match fields, and empty reasons for an existing file without a receipt, matching `inspectConversionFile` without overloading `MAPPING_MISSING`. Added focused PGLite and PGLite/Postgres differential assertions for the exact pre-receipt result.

Fixed in f60e0f85. Chunk validation now uses `SELECT COUNT(*) AS count`, normalizes numeric/string/bigint aggregate representations, and fails closed unless the safe-integer count exactly matches the requested half-open span. The dual-engine suite covers both the valid mapped interval and a gapped/short interval on PGLite and Postgres.

Fixed in f60e0f85. The adapter allowlist is now enforced only at settings depth zero; nested objects and arrays remain recursively bounded and sanitized. Regression coverage accepts/redacts nested values beneath allowed keys, rejects unknown top-level keys, and directly exercises nested array-length and depth limits.

The regression test for the vulnerable pipeline is currently too narrow: it only flags `echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q '` (single-quoted grep arg).
